The condition \( \operatorname{P}(\text{exactly }4\text{ red}) = \operatorname{P}(\text{exactly }5\text{ red}) \) gives

\[
\binom{R}{4}\binom{B}{3} = \binom{R}{5}\binom{B}{2},
\]

where \(R\) and \(B\) are the numbers of red and blue marbles, with \(R+B = n\) and \(R,B \ge 7\). Simplifying,

\[
\frac{\binom{R}{4}}{\binom{R}{5}} = \frac{\binom{B}{2}}{\binom{B}{3}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac{5}{R-4} = \frac{3}{B-2},
\]

so \(5(B-2) = 3(R-4)\). Rearranging yields the linear Diophantine equation

\[
3R - 5B = 2.
\]

A particular solution is \((R,B) = (4,2)\). The general solution is

\[
R = 4 + 5t,\qquad B = 2 + 3t,\qquad t \in \mathbb{Z}.
\]

Then \(n = R+B = 6 + 8t\).

The constraints \(R \ge 7\) and \(B \ge 7\) give

\[
4+5t \ge 7 \;\Rightarrow\; t \ge 1,\qquad 2+3t \ge 7 \;\Rightarrow\; t \ge 2,
\]

so the smallest admissible \(t\) is \(t = 2\). Thus the five smallest values of \(n\) are

\[
t = 2:\; n = 6 + 16 = 22,\quad
t = 3:\; n = 6 + 24 = 30,\quad
t = 4:\; n = 6 + 32 = 38,\quad
t = 5:\; n = 6 + 40 = 46,\quad
t = 6:\; n = 6 + 48 = 54.
\]

Their sum is

\[
22 + 30 + 38 + 46 + 54 = 190.
\]

\[
\boxed{190}
\]
